snapshot.stmt: Can the guarded-district handle be completed into a terminating \(\mathsf{F\text{-}ID}^{+}\) procedure for rational-coefficient qualitative inputs such that every input is first certified feasible or infeasible and every feasible input yields exactly one of the following: a support-guarded exact algebraic certificate \(C\) whose active leaf uniquely certifies \(q_M\) for every \(M\in\mathfrak M\), or an exact algebraic separating certificate \(\mathsf{Sep}\) for two original-alphabet models \(M_0,M_1\in\mathfrak M\) with \(p_{M_0}=p_{M_1}\) and \(q_{M_0}\ne q_{M_1}\)? Guards must be rational-coefficient polynomial sign tests; success leaves may be rational expressions or square-free relations in \(p,q\) with Thom and root-isolation data proving a unique admissible \(q\); failure leaves must encode every CPT entry by an integer minimal polynomial and rational isolating or Thom data and must include exact checks of equal observed laws and unequal targets. The completion must be sound and complete, derive an explicit elementary termination and output-size bound from \(F,J_T,2^K,h,d,m\), use generic real quantifier elimination only to verify returned certificates rather than to search for identification, and embed every successful classical ID output as in the classical-ID embedding proposition without asserting the converse for fixed alphabets. On the overlap of its input language with the finite fixed-alphabet class, this would strictly strengthen only the soundness-only return guarantee of Hwang et al. Theorem 6.1 by adding a total success-or-exact-countermodel guarantee. Relative to Chen--Darwiche Theorem 18 it is a non-comparable fixed-alphabet refinement: joint-treatment positivity implies their separate marginal treatment positivity and is therefore the narrower positivity domain, while preservation of every declared alphabet and a total certificate on both outcomes are orthogonal stronger output requirements.

defs.def:algebraic-separating-certificate: Two original-alphabet CPT families \(\theta^{(0)},\theta^{(1)}\) with every entry encoded by an integer minimal polynomial and a rational isolating interval or Thom encoding, accompanied by exact polynomial and sign checks that both tables belong to \(\mathfrak M\), that \(p_{M_0}=p_{M_1}\), and that at least one coordinate satisfies \(q_{M_0}(t,y)\ne q_{M_1}(t,y)\).
defs.def:fidplus-handle: Start from the exact functional-map feasibility enumerator; refine feasible models by reachable row-support and algebraic strata; propagate denominator licenses bottom-up through sums, products, fractions, marginalization, fixing, and district decomposition; eliminate functional nodes only when their declared alphabets are preserved; encode a successful algebraic leaf by a rational expression or a square-free relation with unique-root Thom data; and turn a terminal failed guarded district into an exact original-alphabet algebraic pair by support-hole row variation or a cardinality-preserving hedge lift. Rational expressions and rational pairs are preferred whenever the stratum admits them.
defs.def:graphwide-fid: \(q\text{ is graphwide }F\text{-identified}\iff\forall M_1,M_2\in\mathfrak M,\ p_{M_1}=p_{M_2}\Rightarrow q_{M_1}=q_{M_2}\).
defs.def:guarded-circuit: A finite decision DAG whose guards are rational-coefficient polynomial tests \(g(p)=0\) or \(g(p)>0\). A success leaf either gives rational arithmetic expressions for every coordinate of \(q\), with each denominator \(b(p)\) licensed by ancestor guards whose conjunction entails \(b(p)>0\) on the compatible-model stratum, or gives square-free rational-coefficient polynomial relations \(H_j(p,q_j)=0\) together with Thom encodings and rational isolating data certifying one unique admissible vector \(q\) in \(\prod_t\Delta(\mathcal A_Y)\).
defs.def:model-class: \(\{M=(G,\mathcal A,\theta): P_M\text{ obeys the recursive product factorization},\ Q_M\text{ obeys truncated intervention semantics},\ \theta_i(\cdot\mid u)\text{ is a point mass for }i\in W,\ P_M(T=t)>0\text{ for every }t\in\mathcal A_T\}\).

assumptions.ass:qualitative-functionality: For every \(i\in W\) and every \(u\in\mathcal A_{\operatorname{pa}_G(i)}\), the row \(\theta_i(\cdot\mid u)\) is a point mass at an unknown state of \(\mathcal A_i\).
assumptions.ass:truncated-intervention: For every \(t\in\mathcal A_T\), the law \(Q_M(t,\cdot)\) is obtained by replacing the rows at vertices in \(T\) by point masses at \(t\) in the product factorization.

snapshot.stmt: In the fixed binary class \(\mathfrak M_{\mathrm w,X}\), where \(A=f(Z)\), suppose \(p_{\mathrm w}(X=x)>0\) for \(x\in\{0,1\}\). The sharp law-specific identified set of \((Q_{X,M}(0,1),Q_{X,M}(1,1))\) is exactly \(\mathcal I(p_{\mathrm w})=[L_0,L_0+M_0]\times[L_1,L_1+M_1]\). Every point of the rectangle is attained by a model using the original binary alphabets, and the vector is point identified if and only if \(p_{zx}>0\) for every \(z\) with \(p_z>0\) and every \(x\in\{0,1\}\).

snapshot.stmt:
Let \(i_Z,i_A,i_X,i_Y\) be distinct vertices and suppose
\(D=\{i_Z,i_A,i_X,i_Y\}\), the edge set of \(G\) is exactly
\[
\{i_Z\mathbin{\to} i_A,\ i_A\mathbin{\to} i_X,
  \ i_A\mathbin{\to} i_Y,\ i_X\mathbin{\to} i_Y\},
\]
\(V=\{i_Z,i_X,i_Y\}\), \(W=\{i_A\}\), \(T=\{i_X\}\), and
\(Y=\{i_Y\}\).  Put
\(\mathcal Z=\mathcal A_{i_Z}\), \(\mathcal B=\mathcal A_{i_A}\),
\(\mathcal X=\mathcal A_{i_X}\), and \(\mathcal Y=\mathcal A_{i_Y}\).
Let \(p\) be a probability law on
\(\mathcal Z\times\mathcal X\times\mathcal Y\).  Put
\(p_X(x)=\sum_{z,y}p(z,x,y)\), and assume \(p_X(x)>0\) for every
\(x\in\mathcal X\).  Write
\(p(z)=\sum_{x,y}p(z,x,y)\) and \(p(z,x)=\sum_y p(z,x,y)\).  Under
the displayed guards define
\[
 e_z(x)=\frac{p(z,x)}{p(z)}\quad\text{when }p(z)>0,
 \qquad
 m_{zx}(y)=\frac{p(z,x,y)}{p(z,x)}\quad\text{when }p(z,x)>0.
\]
For each \(z\) with \(p(z)>0\), define its observed profile by
\[
 \rho_z=\bigl(e_z,(m_{zx})_{x:e_z(x)>0}\bigr).
\]
Thus \(\rho_z=\rho_{z'}\) means that \(e_z=e_{z'}\) and that
\(m_{zx}=m_{z'x}\) for every \(x\) in their common positive support.  Let
\(\mathcal R(p)=\{\rho_z:p(z)>0\}\), and define
\[
 L_x(y)=\sum_{z:p(z,x)>0}p(z)m_{zx}(y),
 \qquad
 M_x=\sum_{z:p(z)>0,\ p(z,x)=0}p(z).
\]
Then the following conclusions hold.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The law \(p\) is the observed marginal of a model in
\(\mathfrak M(G,\mathcal A,V,W,T)\) if and only if
\(\lvert\mathcal R(p)\rvert\leq\lvert\mathcal B\rvert\).  Given an
injection \(\kappa:\mathcal R(p)\to\mathcal B\), an explicit realizing
model sends every positive-mass \(z\) to
\(f(z)=\kappa(\rho_z)\), uses the root row
\(\theta_{i_Z}(z)=p(z)\), uses
\(\theta_{i_X}(\cdot\mid\kappa(\rho_z))=e_z\), and on reached treatment
rows uses \(\theta_{i_Y}(\cdot\mid\kappa(\rho_z),x)=m_{zx}\).  Zero-root-mass,
unused-state, and unreached outcome rows may be filled by arbitrary
probability vectors.  If \(p\) is rational, all arbitrary rows can be
chosen rational, giving a rational realizing model on the original
alphabets.
\item On every feasible law, the sharp identified set of the full
single-treatment intervention vector is
\[
 \mathcal Q(p)
 :=\left\{\bigl(Q_M(x,\cdot)\bigr)_{x\in\mathcal X}:
 M\in\mathfrak M(G,\mathcal A,V,W,T),\ p_M=p\right\}
 =\prod_{x\in\mathcal X}\bigl(L_x+M_x\Delta(\mathcal Y)\bigr),
\]
where \(L_x=(L_x(y))_{y\in\mathcal Y}\).  Simultaneous attainment is
obtained in the model above by setting, for every assigned profile whose
\(X\)-row misses \(x\), the common outcome row
\[
 s_x=\frac{q_x-L_x}{M_x}\quad\text{when }M_x>0
\]
for a desired \(q_x\in L_x+M_x\Delta(\mathcal Y)\); when \(M_x=0\), the
row is irrelevant and may be arbitrary.  The choices are independent
across \(x\).  If both \(p\) and the desired vector \(q\) are rational,
this attaining model can be chosen rational.
\item The full vector is point identified if and only if either
\(\lvert\mathcal Y\rvert=1\), or \(M_x=0\) for every
\(x\in\mathcal X\).  Hence, when \(\lvert\mathcal Y\rvert\geq2\), point
identification holds exactly when \(p(z,x)>0\) for every \(z\) with
\(p(z)>0\) and every \(x\in\mathcal X\).
\item After exact comparison of the profiles, feasibility, all
\(L_x(y)\) and \(M_x\), and the point-collapse test require
\(O(\lvert\mathcal Z\rvert\lvert\mathcal X\rvert
\lvert\mathcal Y\rvert)\) guarded arithmetic operations.  The region has
the linear-size half-space representation
\[
 q_x(y)\geq L_x(y)\quad(x\in\mathcal X,\ y\in\mathcal Y),
 \qquad
 \sum_{y\in\mathcal Y}q_x(y)=1\quad(x\in\mathcal X).
\]
\end{enumerate}

snapshot.stmt:
Let \(D=\{Z,A,X,Y\}\), let \(\mathcal A_Z,\mathcal A_A,\mathcal A_X,\mathcal A_Y\) be arbitrary fixed finite nonempty alphabets, and let \(G\) have precisely the edges \(Z\to A\), \(A\to X\), \(A\to Y\), and \(X\to Y\).  Set \(V=\{Z,X,Y\}\), \(H=\{A\}\), \(W=\{A\}\), \(T=\{Z,X\}\), and take the outcome set to be \(\{Y\}\).  For every \(M\in\mathfrak M(G,\mathcal A,V,W,T)\), every \(z\in\mathcal A_Z\), every \(x\in\mathcal A_X\), and every \(y\in\mathcal A_Y\), joint-treatment positivity entails \(p_M(z,x)>0\), and
\[
 P_M(Y=y\mid do(Z=z,X=x))
 =\frac{p_M(z,x,y)}{p_M(z,x)}
 =p_M(Y=y\mid Z=z,X=x).
\]
Thus the complete joint-intervention distribution is graphwide identified by a guarded conditional-probability circuit for arbitrary fixed finite alphabets.

snapshot.stmt:
Let \(i_Z,i_A,i_X,i_Y\) be distinct vertices, put
\(\iota=(i_Z,i_A,i_X,i_Y)\), and suppose that
\(D=\{i_Z,i_A,i_X,i_Y\}\), that the edge set of \(G\) is exactly
\[
 \{i_Z\mathbin{\to}i_A,\ i_A\mathbin{\to}i_X,
   \ i_A\mathbin{\to}i_Y,\ i_X\mathbin{\to}i_Y\},
\]
that \(V=\{i_Z,i_X,i_Y\}\), \(W=\{i_A\}\),
\(T=\{i_Z,i_X\}\), and \(Y=\{i_Y\}\).  Write
\(\mathcal Z=\mathcal A_{i_Z}\), \(\mathcal B=\mathcal A_{i_A}\),
\(\mathcal X=\mathcal A_{i_X}\), \(\mathcal Y=\mathcal A_{i_Y}\),
and \(B=\lvert\mathcal B\rvert\).  Let \(p\) be a law on
\(\mathcal Z\times\mathcal X\times\mathcal Y\) satisfying the separate
coordinate positivity conditions
\[
 p(z)>0\quad(z\in\mathcal Z),
 \qquad p_X(x)>0\quad(x\in\mathcal X).
\]
Use the guarded profiles, the profile-refinement partitions
\(\Pi_B(p)\), the response-kernel region \(\mathcal K(p)\), and the
saturation threshold \(B_{\mathrm{sat}}(p)\) from Definitions
\(\mathrm{def:profile\text{-}refinement\text{-}kernel\text{-}region}\)
and \(\mathrm{def:saturation\text{-}alphabet\text{-}threshold}\).  For a
model \(M\), define the causal response kernel
\[
 K_M(z,x,y)=P_M(i_Y=y\mid do(i_Z=z,i_X=x)).
\]
Then the following statements hold.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The law \(p\) is induced by a model in
\(\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{sep}}(G,\mathcal A,V,W,T,Y;\iota)\) if and only if
\(R:=\lvert\mathcal R(p)\rvert\leq B\).  On a feasible observed-law
fiber, the partitions of \(\mathcal Z\) into the nonempty fibers of the
functional map \(f:\mathcal Z\to\mathcal B\) are exactly
\(\Pi_B(p)\): the map may split an observed-profile class but may never
merge two distinct observed-profile classes.
\item On every feasible law, the sharp, simultaneously attainable set of
the full response kernel is
\[
 \left\{K_M:M\in
 \mathfrak M_{\mathrm{sep}}(G,\mathcal A,V,W,T,Y;\iota),\ p_M=p\right\}
 =\mathcal K(p)
 =\bigcup_{\pi\in\Pi_B(p)}\mathcal K_\pi(p).
\]
Every point is attained without changing any alphabet.  If \(p\) and the
selected kernel are rational, an attaining model can be chosen with
rational conditional tables.
\item Suppose \(R\leq B\).  At \(B=R\), the only admissible partition is
the partition into observed-profile classes, so for each profile \(\rho\)
and each \(x\in H_\rho\) there is one common free row shared by all
\(z\) having profile \(\rho\).  If \(\lvert\mathcal Y\rvert\geq2\), then
\[
 B_{\mathrm{sat}}(p)
 =R+\sum_{\rho:H_\rho\ne\varnothing}
 \bigl(\lvert\{z:\rho_z=\rho\}\rvert-1\bigr)
\]
is the least hidden-alphabet cardinality for which every missing
\((z,x)\) response row can vary independently.  More precisely, for
\[
 \mathcal K_{\mathrm{ind}}(p)
 =\left\{k:
 \begin{array}{ll}
 k(z,x,\cdot)=m_{zx},&e_z(x)>0,\\
 k(z,x,\cdot)\in\Delta(\mathcal Y)\text{ independently},&e_z(x)=0,
 \end{array}\right\},
\]
the region with hidden cardinality \(b\) equals
\(\mathcal K_{\mathrm{ind}}(p)\) for every
\(b\geq B_{\mathrm{sat}}(p)\), and is a strict subset for
\(R\leq b<B_{\mathrm{sat}}(p)\).  Intermediate cardinalities give exactly
the displayed finite union of profile-refinement polytopes.
\item On a feasible law, the full response kernel is point identified if
and only if either \(\lvert\mathcal Y\rvert=1\), or
\(p(z,x)>0\) for every \((z,x)\in\mathcal Z\times\mathcal X\).
\item Let \(Q_M^X(x,\cdot)=P_M(i_Y\in\cdot\mid do(i_X=x))\).  Projection
of the response kernel gives
\[
 Q_M^X(x,\cdot)=\sum_{z\in\mathcal Z}p(z)K_M(z,x,\cdot),
\]
and its sharp region is
\[
 \prod_{x\in\mathcal X}\bigl(L_x+M_x\Delta(\mathcal Y)\bigr),
 \quad
 L_x(y)=\sum_{z:p(z,x)>0}p(z)m_{zx}(y),
 \quad
 M_x=\sum_{z:p(z,x)=0}p(z).
\]
If, in addition, joint positivity \(p(z,x)>0\) holds for every
\((z,x)\), then \(\mathcal K(p)\) is the singleton guarded circuit
\[
 K_M(z,x,y)=m_{zx}(y)=\frac{p(z,x,y)}{p(z,x)}.
\]
\item The family \(\Pi_B(p)\) can be enumerated by at most
\(B^{\lvert\mathcal Z\rvert}\) labeled block assignments after exact
profile comparison.  Each \(\mathcal K_\pi(p)\) has
\(O(\lvert\mathcal Z\rvert\lvert\mathcal X\rvert
\lvert\mathcal Y\rvert)\) simplex inequalities and linear equalities,
and all conditional divisions are guarded by the tested strict
denominators \(p(z)>0\) or \(p(z,x)>0\).
\end{enumerate}

defs.def:profile-refinement-kernel-region:
Fix the four-node notation \(\iota=(i_Z,i_A,i_X,i_Y)\), put
\(\mathcal Z=\mathcal A_{i_Z}\), \(\mathcal B=\mathcal A_{i_A}\),
\(\mathcal X=\mathcal A_{i_X}\), and
\(\mathcal Y=\mathcal A_{i_Y}\), and let \(p\) be a law on
\(\mathcal Z\times\mathcal X\times\mathcal Y\) with \(p(z)>0\) for every
\(z\).  Define, under the displayed positive denominators,
\[
 e_z(x)=\frac{p(z,x)}{p(z)},
 \qquad
 m_{zx}(y)=\frac{p(z,x,y)}{p(z,x)}\quad\text{when }p(z,x)>0,
\]
and
\[
 \rho_z=\bigl(e_z,(m_{zx})_{x:e_z(x)>0}\bigr),
 \qquad
 \mathcal R(p)=\{\rho_z:z\in\mathcal Z\}.
\]
For an integer \(b\geq1\), let \(\Pi_b(p)\) be the set of partitions
\(\pi\) of \(\mathcal Z\) with at most \(b\) nonempty blocks such that
every block is contained in one set \(\{z:\rho_z=\rho\}\).  For
\(\pi\in\Pi_b(p)\), let \(\mathcal K_\pi(p)\) be the set of arrays
\(k=(k(z,x,\cdot))_{z,x}\) of elements of \(\Delta(\mathcal Y)\) such
that, for every block \(C\in\pi\),
\[
 k(z,x,\cdot)=m_{zx}\quad\text{if }e_z(x)>0,
\]
and, if \(e_z(x)=0\) for \(z\in C\), there is one
\(s_{C,x}\in\Delta(\mathcal Y)\) satisfying
\[
 k(z,x,\cdot)=s_{C,x}\quad\text{for every }z\in C.
\]
The separate-positive response-kernel region is
\[
 \mathcal K(p)=
 \bigcup_{\pi\in\Pi_{|\mathcal B|}(p)}\mathcal K_\pi(p).
\]
defs.def:saturation-alphabet-threshold:
In the notation of
Definition \(\mathrm{def:profile\text{-}refinement\text{-}kernel\text{-}region}\),
put
\[
 H_\rho=\{x\in\mathcal X:e_z(x)=0\text{ for, equivalently every, }
 z\text{ with }\rho_z=\rho\},
\]
and define
\[
 B_{\mathrm{sat}}(p)
 =|\mathcal R(p)|+
 \sum_{\rho\in\mathcal R(p):H_\rho\ne\varnothing}
 \bigl(|\{z\in\mathcal Z:\rho_z=\rho\}|-1\bigr).
\]
defs.def:separate-positive-four-node-class:
For an ordered quadruple \(\iota=(i_Z,i_A,i_X,i_Y)\) of distinct
vertices, \(\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{sep}}(G,\mathcal A,V,W,T,Y;\iota)\) is
the set of recursive models \(M=(G,\mathcal A,\theta)\) for which
\(D=\{i_Z,i_A,i_X,i_Y\}\), the edge set is
\(\{i_Z\to i_A,i_A\to i_X,i_A\to i_Y,i_X\to i_Y\}\),
\(V=\{i_Z,i_X,i_Y\}\), \(W=\{i_A\}\),
\(T=\{i_Z,i_X\}\), and \(Y=\{i_Y\}\); the observational law obeys the
recursive product factorization, interventions obey the truncated product
factorization, every row at \(i_A\) is a point mass, and
\[
 P_M(i_Z=z)>0\quad(z\in\mathcal A_{i_Z}),
 \qquad
 P_M(i_X=x)>0\quad(x\in\mathcal A_{i_X}).
\]
No condition \(P_M(i_Z=z,i_X=x)>0\) is imposed.

assumptions.ass:qualitative-functionality: For every \(i\in W\) and every \(u\in\mathcal A_{\operatorname{pa}_G(i)}\), the row \(\theta_i(\cdot\mid u)\) is a point mass at an unknown state of \(\mathcal A_i\).
assumptions.ass:truncated-intervention: For every \(t\in\mathcal A_T\), the law \(Q_M(t,\cdot)\) is obtained by replacing the rows at vertices in \(T\) by point masses at \(t\) in the product factorization.
